hints: A permutation splits into disjoint cycles; a cycle of length L returns to its start every L rounds.
The full array returns when the round count is divisible by every cycle length.
The first such round is the least common multiple, which can be too large to store directly.
analogy: Each cycle has its own rotation period; combine their prime factors using the largest exponent needed.
example: Cycles of lengths 4 and 6 need lcm(4,6)=12 rounds to return together.
correctness: A position returns exactly at multiples of its cycle length, so the earliest common return contains each prime to the largest exponent found in any cycle.
complexity: O(n sqrt n) with trial factoring (or O(n log n) with SPF) and O(n) storage; modular multiplication avoids overflow.
algorithm: Find all cycle lengths. Factor each with a smallest-prime-factor table and retain the maximum exponent of each prime across all cycles. Multiply p^e modulo 1,000,000,007 for those maxima; never compute the potentially huge LCM directly.
